exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Escape to Host
exploitedBy.relevance: Excessive Linux capabilities (e.g., CAP_SYS_ADMIN) directly enable container escape to the host.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Container Administration Command
exploitedBy.relevance: Granted capabilities allow execution of privileged administration commands within or beyond the container boundary.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Ptrace System Calls
exploitedBy.relevance: A missing seccomp profile allows unrestricted ptrace syscalls, enabling process injection and container escape.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Kernel Modules and Extensions
exploitedBy.relevance: Permissive seccomp profiles allow loading of kernel modules, enabling persistent host-level compromise.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Inter-Process Communication
exploitedBy.relevance: Shared IPC namespace allows cross-container inter-process communication, breaking zone isolation.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Container Service
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak LSM enforcement allows attackers to manipulate or create container services without policy restrictions.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Trust Dependencies
exploitedBy.relevance: Unrestricted egress allows attackers to exploit network trust relationships and propagate across trust boundaries.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Boundary Bridging
exploitedBy.relevance: Unrestricted egress enables bridging of network boundaries, allowing lateral movement between zones.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Trust Modification
exploitedBy.relevance: Permissive ingress policies can reflect or enable modification of trust relationships between network zones.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Unsecured Credentials
exploitedBy.relevance: Credentials stored in environment variables represent unsecured credentials accessible to any process in the container.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Credentials In Files
exploitedBy.relevance: Environment variable credentials can be exposed through /proc or mounted filesystems, similar to credentials in files.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Container API
exploitedBy.relevance: Over-projected service account tokens provide excessive API access credentials accessible within the container.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Steal Application Access Token
exploitedBy.relevance: Projected service account tokens are application access tokens that can be stolen and reused by attackers.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Additional Container Cluster Roles
exploitedBy.relevance: Over-projected tokens with excessive roles grant attackers additional cluster-level permissions if compromised.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Hide Infrastructure
exploitedBy.relevance: Unmonitored traffic paths allow attackers to hide malicious inter-zone communication from defenders.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Sniffing
exploitedBy.relevance: Without monitoring, network sniffing on inter-zone paths goes undetected, enabling credential and data capture.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Traffic Signaling
exploitedBy.relevance: Unmonitored paths can be used for covert traffic signaling between compromised nodes across zones.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: System Network Connections Discovery
exploitedBy.relevance: Access to the host network namespace allows enumeration of all system network connections on the host.
